clue.text: Egg-beater to help rice stirring

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of the three words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook beats eggs, mixing in some rice to help the dish along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg-beater' looks like a kitchen whisk, but it is slang for a rotor aircraft; 'stirring' shuffles TO HELP RICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-beater is informal slang for a rotorcraft, from the whirling blades.

clue.text: Remove a draught in mood of anger

explanation.surface: Someone shuts out a cold draught while in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draught' reads as a cold breeze, but it is a piece in the board game draughts, which Americans call checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard senses of the same word: a penalty capture in draughts and a fit of petulant annoyance.

clue.text: Jemmy, for instance, turned to get plunder

indicators.note: turned round, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a jemmy (crowbar) is an example of a tool

explanation.surface: A burglar's crowbar is put to use to get the swag.
explanation.walkthrough: A jemmy is a burglar's short crowbar, which fits the surface's theft scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is stolen goods, a synonym of plunder as a noun.

clue.text: Six planes appear often in this art form

definitions.text: Six planes appear often in this art form

parts.words: Six planes appear often in this art form
parts.note: a solid with six plane faces gives its name to a modernist painting style built from geometric shapes

explanation.surface: Aircraft keep turning up in some style of painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planes' suggests aircraft but means flat faces: a cube has six, and the Picasso–Braque movement is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The early twentieth-century art movement takes its name from the six-faced solid its paintings fragment things into.

clue.text: Playing a sly trick like a reck less batsman

definitions.meaning: a cricketer who hooks or pulls a quick delivery from the bowler rashly

explanation.surface: A cricketer bats recklessly and pulls off some cunning deception.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'fast one' is a quick ball and to 'pull' is to hit it across to the leg side; the OCR splits 'reckless' in two.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means deceiving someone; literally it describes a batter hitting a quick delivery.

clue.text: Protector of the orb

parts.note: the orb is the eyeball, and the fold of skin that closes over it guards it

explanation.surface: A guardian of the royal orb among the crown jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orb' suggests the monarch's regalia, but it is a poetic word for the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin fold that closes over the eyeball shields it, and orb is a literary term for the eye.

clue.text: In the middle of a motorway, driver's first

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Half way along a motorway, the leading motorist is in the thick of the traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning surrounded by or among.

clue.text: Flat at Eton semi-converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A flat in a half-converted building at the famous school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Semi' looks like half of 'semi-converted', but it is fodder; 'converted' turns AT ETON SEMI into the answer. A semi is also a British semi-detached house, adding to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a flat on two floors with its own entrance, a kind of apartment.

clue.text: Free to ring back, having ring back?

definitions.meaning: a telephone line not busy, so one can call again
having handed back the betrothal ring, no longer promised in marriage

explanation.surface: Someone is free to return a call, having got their ring returned.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'ring' is a phone call and the second a betrothal ring; a line that is not busy is free, and a couple who return the ring are no longer betrothed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means not busy on a phone line, and also released from a promise to marry.

clue.text: He hopes to make passes without giving offence

definitions.text: He hopes to make passes without giving offence

parts.words: He hopes to make passes without giving offence
parts.note: reads like a polite would-be suitor, but describes a sportsman passing the ball without committing fouls

explanation.surface: A shy admirer hopes to flirt without causing offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make passes' suggests flirting and 'offence' rudeness, but they are passing the ball and committing a foul on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A soccer player passes the ball to teammates and tries to avoid fouls.

clue.text: Time-signal from Seville

definitions.meaning: the BBC radio sequence of short beeps marking the hour
seeds found in Seville oranges, the bitter fruit used for marmalade

explanation.surface: A Spanish city broadcasts its hourly radio signal.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC broadcasts six short beeps on the hour, known by this name; Seville oranges are full of seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: The short beeps of the radio time signal share their name with small fruit seeds.

clue.text: Odd fete Sid disrupted in Wales

definitions.text: Odd fete Sid disrupted in Wales

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sid spoils a strange village fete held in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disrupted' shuffles ODD FETE SID; the whole clue describes the festival, an odd fete in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh festival of music and poetry is a kind of fete held in Wales.

clue.text: Top dressing applied after stubble is cleared

parts.note: removing bristles from the face with a razor is a shave

explanation.surface: A farmer spreads fertiliser on a field after clearing the stubble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top dressing' and 'stubble' suggest farming, but the stubble is on a chin and the dressing is lotion slapped on afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A scented lotion is dabbed on the face, the body's top, after a razor has been used.

clue.text: Hoping endlessly for an analgesic

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone keeps hoping for a painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: This common drug relieves pain, which is what an analgesic does.

clue.text: Powder-room of football team

definitions.meaning: a store for gunpowder and weapons

explanation.surface: The ladies' room belonging to a soccer club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powder-room' suggests a ladies' lavatory but means a store of gunpowder; Arsenal is a London soccer club named after the Woolwich armoury.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a weapons store and is also the name of a London soccer club.

clue.text: Love of ear of African flower

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, nil
otic is the adjective meaning of the ear

explanation.surface: Fondness for an ear of some flower from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword code for a river, here the Nile: something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the Nile, the great river of Africa.

clue.text: Rat fit for racing

definitions.meaning: to rat is to tell tales or betray to the authorities
in good condition, ready to race, as a horse on recent form

explanation.surface: A rodent is in shape to race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' looks like a noun but is the verb for betraying someone; read as two words, the answer means on form.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to snitch, and split as a phrase it means in good condition.

clue.text: Abandon pig amid noise

indicators.note: amid means surrounded by, so the pig word goes inside the noise word

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a pig behind amid the racket.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown is to reject or cast off, a synonym of abandon.

clue.text: But did its singers touch the audience?

definitions.text: But did its singers touch the audience?

parts.words: But did its singers touch the audience?
parts.note: touch is slang for asking for money, so performers who are cadgers might hit up the audience for cash

explanation.surface: A critic asks whether the cast moved the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch' means move emotionally on the surface, but 'to touch someone' is also to beg money from them; the singers in John Gay's 1728 ballad opera are beggars.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gay's ballad opera is peopled by vagrants and thieves, who might cadge money from listeners.

clue.text: Part of nudism always depressing

indicators.note: part of means the answer is a run of letters inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Naturism is always a gloomy business.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal means gloomy, a synonym of depressing.

clue.text: Boundaries of motorway in French retirement places

indicators.note: in places the motorway letter inside the French word

parts.note: lits are French beds, where one retires at night

explanation.surface: The edges of a motorway in France where people go to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement places' suggests old people's homes, but retiring here is going to bed, French lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Limits are the bounds or borders of something, synonyms of boundaries.

clue.text: Word of advice to member-walk stealthily!

parts.note: a tip is a useful hint
a toe is a member, a part of the body

explanation.surface: A warning whispered to a club member: creep quietly!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a club member, but in crosswords it often means a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To tiptoe is to move quietly on the balls of the feet, creeping without noise.

clue.text: Signs put up by se or in Espana?

definitions.text: Signs put up by se or in Espana?

parts.words: Signs put up by se or in Espana?
parts.note: the wavy marks a Spaniard places over n, as in señor and España

explanation.surface: Notices posted by a gentleman in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signs put up' suggests notices, but these are the wavy accents placed over n in Spanish; the OCR has dropped them, printing 'se or' and 'Espana'.
explanation.definitionFit: The wavy diacritic over the Spanish ñ is what these marks are.

clue.text: Very old rock bands from Class II

indicators.note: from here means the answer is made out of the letters of the words that follow, rearranged

explanation.surface: Ageing rockers are made of second-class stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock bands' suggests ageing musicians, but they are geological strata of the Lias, an early Jurassic rock series.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes strata of the Lias, an early Jurassic layer of rock, so very ancient bands of stone.

clue.text: French always in battle

parts.note: ay is a poetic word for always

explanation.surface: The French are forever in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: AY (also spelt aye) is an old word for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a fight or skirmish, as in joining the fray.

clue.text: Right honourable

explanation.surface: The formal title of a Privy Counsellor or MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right Honourable' is the style of a British Privy Counsellor, but split into two words each gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means correct and also loyal or upright.

clue.text: Indian farmer said to be in civil commotion

indicators.note: said to be means the word sounds like the one that follows when spoken

parts.note: a riot is a disturbance of public order

explanation.surface: A peasant from India reportedly caught up in unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: A ryot is a tenant cultivator in India, a word from the Raj.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a ryot is a peasant cultivator or tenant tiller of the land.

clue.text: Dry soldier can become so unruly

indicators.note: can become means the letters may turn into a new word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thirsty soldier may become rowdy.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorderly means unruly or rowdy, out of control.

clue.text: Sea-bass?

definitions.meaning: a poetic name for the ocean
a bass voice is low in pitch

explanation.surface: A fish species is named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea-bass' reads as a fish, but the hyphen splits two definitions: the ocean, and a low voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a poetic noun for the ocean and describes a low-pitched voice.

clue.text: Chaps on donkeys take time to make judgment

annotationWithheld.why: Chaps on donkeys take time to make judgment: MEN on ASSES plus T gives ASSESMENT, one S short of ASSESSMENT; no reading supplies the second S
annotationWithheld.clue: Chaps on donkeys take time to make judgment
